subject: Day 3: first-week visit window opens; jaundice peak begins
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 3. The first-week pediatrician visit window opens today (day 3-5). Stool should now look green-brown to mustard-yellow if breastfeeding, or tan if formula-feeding. Target output: at least three wet diapers and three stools today. Weight nadir is typically day 3-5 — Avi will likely weigh less today than at birth, which is expected if it stays within 7%.

Action items
- Bring Avi to the first-week visit if scheduled today. The pediatrician will check weight, jaundice level, latch, and feeding effectiveness. Bring the feeding log. AAP Bright Futures periodicity schedule: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Ask the pediatrician to assess transcutaneous bilirubin if jaundice is visible past the face. Bilirubin nomogram thresholds depend on age in hours and risk factors. AAP HealthyChildren on jaundice: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Jaundice.aspx
- Continue the feeding log. Add latch quality notes (LATCH score or just "good/struggling") for the IBCLC if you are seeing one.
- If you have not yet applied for Avi's Social Security number, submit the SS-5 form today. Mail takes 2-4 weeks. SSA application: https://www.ssa.gov/ssnumber/
- Add Avi to your health insurance — if you have not started this, today is the day. Hard 30-day window. Healthcare.gov QLE reference: https://www.healthcare.gov/glossary/qualifying-life-event/

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Weight loss up to 7% of birth weight; bilirubin rising visibly on the face; baby acne or milia; occasional sneezes or hiccups.
- [low concern] Stool now green-brown or mustard-yellow (breastfed) or tan (formula).
- [monitor] Weight loss 7-10%; the pediatrician will assess feeding effectiveness today. Yellow tinge limited to the face is physiologic; below the chest is not.
- [call within 24h] Yellow tinge spreading from face to chest and belly. Fewer than four wet diapers in a day. Persistent inability to latch. Weight loss greater than 10%.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). In infants under 90 days this is a workup-required event, full stop. Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunity
Live human voice during awake-alert windows. Sing, hum, or read aloud — content irrelevant. The active ingredient is the prosody and cadence of live voice, which the auditory cortex preferentially encodes over recorded audio. Trainor LJ et al. (Dev Sci 2012) on live vs passive music exposure in infants: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22356269/

Upcoming
- Day 5-15: cord stump dries and detaches.
- Day 7-10: weight check; most regain birth weight by day 14.
- Day 14-21: first common growth spurt.
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit window opens.

Further reading
- Cribsheet by Emily Oster — evidence-based decisions from birth to preschool: https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/562146/cribsheet-by-emily-oster/
- The Happiest Baby on the Block by Harvey Karp — soothing fundamentals: https://www.happiestbaby.com/pages/dr-harvey-karp
- AAP HealthyChildren overview of the first month: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- CDC on newborn screening for parents: https://www.cdc.gov/newborn-screening/about/index.html
